tasks.short: Dress in protective clothing and breathing apparatus

steps.what: Dress with fire-resistant clothing and breathing apparatus and check fit

tasks.design: Keep donning and physical fit checks with the firefighter under the existing equipment procedure. References in {DOCS} can support training, but no software change reduces preparation or checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment must be physically donned and checked on the wearer.
tasks.enabler_now: A digital procedure does not perform dressing or establish correct fit.
tasks.still_hard: Noticing a fit, seal or equipment problem before exposure.
tasks.human_edge: The wearer can feel a problem, inspect equipment and request assistance.
tasks.altitude: Physical preparation and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of firefighting and prevention workers
reach.task: Resolve an equipment-readiness concern before deployment

evidence.claim: Software references do not remove physical donning and fit checks; this unchanged design claims no labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is dressing and immediate equipment checks, not inventory logs or incident reports.
Firefighter produces donned equipment and checks it in s1; no automated readiness flag is assumed.
Check native training-reference access before future custom work.
No new software, logging or maintained dataset is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Equipment types and local readiness procedures
research_questions: Which equipment issues require assistance rather than a different instruction format?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0 give zero saving. Routine dressing and equipment-fit difficulties retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Approach a fire using scene and building knowledge

steps.what: Assess types of fires, construction, materials and physical layout
Move toward the source of a fire under incident command

tasks.design: Retain scene assessment and physical movement with the firefighter within incident command. Existing building references in {DOCS} remain supporting information, with no assumption that a digital layout is current or replaces live assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Conditions can change and available building information may not match the scene.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest's reporting tools establish no safe automated approach capability.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling limited visibility, construction knowledge and changing conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The firefighter can notice a contradiction, communicate it and reconsider the approach with the crew.
tasks.altitude: No change to operational decision rights or approach time.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of firefighting and prevention workers
reach.task: Clarify conflicting scene and building information

evidence.claim: Operational approach requires current scene judgement and physical movement; no reporting capability establishes a labour saving for it.

assumptions: Boundary is scene assessment and approach, not dispatch priority, route planning to the site or later reporting.
Firefighter produces situational assessment in s1 before acting in s2. Existing incident instructions are an input, not a new automated decision.
No structured safe-route or building-condition flag is assumed; unavailable information remains uncertain.
Native reference access should be assessed before future custom code. This unchanged process introduces no upkeep.
unknowns: Local incident command and information access arrangements
research_questions: How are discrepancies between building references and observed conditions communicated?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100 with no upkeep give zero saving. Both familiar and uncertain properties retain assessment and movement time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain dispatcher contact about resources and difficulties

steps.what: Maintain contact with fire dispatchers about additional firefighters, supplies and difficulties

tasks.design: Keep incident radio contact through the operational communications equipment {OTHER}. The firefighter communicates and confirms needs; no bot classifies urgency, places a resource request or replaces acknowledgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Resource needs and difficulties depend on changing conditions and require shared understanding.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing radio communication remains the means; reporting dashboards do not replace operational conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Communicating clearly under noise and uncertainty while confirming what was understood.
tasks.human_edge: The firefighter can clarify ambiguity and explain a difficulty that a status code misses.
tasks.altitude: Contact time and command boundaries remain unchanged.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of firefighting and prevention workers
reach.task: Clarify an operational resource request within command arrangements
reach.learn: Closed communication and resource authority boundaries

evidence.claim: Resource requests and incident difficulties require live communication and acknowledgement; no saving is assumed from existing radio runtime.

assumptions: Boundary is firefighter contact; dispatcher allocation labour is outside the focal role and is neither removed nor transferred.
Firefighter produces resource needs and difficulty descriptions during s1; no structured incident-class input or automated urgency judgement is assumed.
Assess native communication tools before future custom code; no operational channel changes are proposed.
There is no new recording, monitoring or maintained dataset, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Local communications protocol and resource-request authority
research_questions: Which contact failures arise from ambiguous information rather than the communication channel?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0 give zero saving. Routine updates and urgent requests retain contact and clarification time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain firefighting knowledge through practice and professional learning

steps.what: Maintain firefighting practices by participating in drills
Attend seminars, conventions, and conferences on current firefighting practices

tasks.design: Retain drills and professional learning time. Existing materials in {LMS} or {DOCS} can support study, but an automatic summary is not treated as equivalent to practice or participation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Competence requires rehearsal, feedback and understanding of current practices.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital access can aid learning without demonstrating shorter practice time.
tasks.still_hard: Applying lessons to local equipment and coordinated crew action.
tasks.human_edge: The firefighter can test understanding, ask questions and learn from colleagues' experience.
tasks.altitude: Learning commitment and competence requirements remain unchanged.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of firefighting and prevention workers
reach.task: Discuss a learning need identified during a drill
reach.learn: Feedback interpretation and authorised practice changes

evidence.claim: Practice and professional learning retain participation effort; digital summaries alone do not establish equivalent competence or time savings.

assumptions: Boundary is learning and practice, excluding enrolment scheduling and certificate administration.
Firefighter produces learning needs in s1 and learning outcomes through participation; no machine-certified competence score is assumed.
Review native learning-reference facilities before custom development.
No new learning service or maintained content is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Required drill frequency and local learning standards
research_questions: Which learning needs require practical rehearsal rather than more reading material?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0 give zero saving. Routine refreshers and new practices retain learning time; enrolment administration is outside the boundary.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Operational preparation, approach, dispatcher contact and professional learning retain their time and authority boundaries.
reach: Help supervisors recognise equipment, information and learning concerns early
role.ambitious_version: A firefighter who communicates uncertainty clearly and maintains practical competence within incident command.
